The mijwiz is a traditional aerophone of West Asia and the Middle East from the Levant (Palestine, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan); the Arabic name means 'double'. It is made of two short bamboo pipes of equal length joined at the reed end, and belongs to the double-pipe single-reed woodwinds, Hornbostel–Sachs number 422.221.2. Each pipe has about five or six fingerholes, and playing it requires circular breathing to keep the sound continuous. In the Levant it accompanies belly dance or dabke, the folk line dance, and it is also common in folk song recordings and in song lyrics, for example the Lebanese singer Sabah's dabke song 《Jeeb el Mijwiz ya Abboud》.
米日維茲雙管由兩根等長的管子組成，每根管子上約有五至六個小孔用於指法演奏。演奏此: The mijwiz is made of two pipes of equal length, each with about five to six small holes for fingering. Playing it needs the special technique of circular breathing, which is difficult but produces a continuous tone without pausing to take breath. In the Levant the mijwiz accompanies belly dance or dabke, the Levantine line dance. Many folk song recordings include the mijwiz, and song lyrics mention the instrument by name. A famous example is the dabke song 《傑布埃爾米日維茲亞阿布德》 (Jeeb el Mijwiz ya Abboud), sung by the Lebanese singer Sabah. The mijwiz is related to the arghul, which consists of one short and one long pipe, similar in construction to the mijwiz and close in timbre. Both are related to the ancestor instruments of some bagpipes: the player uses circular breathing so that the cheeks act as the bag that stores air in a bagpipe.
米日維茲雙管由竹子製成，包括兩根等長的短竹管作為主體。竹管頂端裝配蘆葦片（簧片）: The mijwiz is made of bamboo: two short bamboo pipes of equal length form the body. At the top of each pipe is a reed, usually of natural cane, which vibrates to make the sound. Each pipe is bored with five to six small holes that control the pitch by fingering. Bamboo, being naturally hollow and resonant, is an ideal material for a wind instrument, and it is light and durable, so it lasts well in the climate of the Middle East.
米日維茲雙管音色明亮尖銳，具有穿透力強的特徵。其音質帶有溫暖的鼻音共鳴，在中高音: The mijwiz has a bright, sharp timbre that carries well. Its tone has a warm nasal resonance and is strong in the upper middle register, without being too harsh or too heavy. The double-pipe design produces a natural harmonic effect, and the two reeds sounding at once create a distinctive shimmer and depth.
音域範圍相對有限，主要集中在中音至高音區。其共鳴方式較為直接，依賴蘆葦片的振動和: Its range is fairly limited, mostly from the middle to the upper register. It resonates in a fairly direct way, relying on the vibration of the cane reeds and on the resonance of the air column inside the bamboo pipes. Compared with the Arab flute, the mijwiz sounds thicker; compared with the Western clarinet, it sounds plainer and more local, with a strong flavour of the Levant. Its overall sound is intimate, which suits folk songs and traditional music.
